explanation: Zinc, being more reactive than copper, displaces copper from copper sulphate solution, forming zinc sulphate and depositing metallic copper.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: Grey zinc granules or a strip, in a deep blue copper sulphate solution.
beaker_view.final_appearance: A colourless zinc sulphate solution, with the zinc now coated in reddish-brown copper.
beaker_view.observation: The deep blue solution fades to colourless as the zinc surface picks up a visible reddish-brown coating of displaced copper.
